reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Calling discitis a Modic type 1 change without considering the clinical picture.
name: Modic Endplate Changes

version.label: Modic et al. (1988), types 1–3
version.detail: Classified by T1 and T2 signal of the endplate and adjacent marrow. Mixed types (e.g. 1/2) are described as such.

purpose: Classifies degenerative vertebral endplate and marrow signal changes on MRI.

options.label: Type 1: oedema / inflammation
options.detail: Low T1 and high T2 signal in the vertebral endplate and marrow.

options.label: Type 2: fatty replacement
options.detail: High T1 and iso- to high T2 signal.

options.label: Type 3: sclerosis
options.detail: Low T1 and low T2 signal.

resultStates.label: Type 1: oedema / inflammation
resultStates.summary: Low T1 and high T2 signal in the vertebral endplate and marrow.

resultStates.label: Type 2: fatty replacement
resultStates.summary: High T1 and iso- to high T2 signal.

resultStates.label: Type 3: sclerosis
resultStates.summary: Low T1 and low T2 signal.

clinicalContext.text: Type 1 changes are the most often associated with low back pain.

clinicalInsights.text: Type 1 changes can resemble infection; correlate clinically and with the disc.

limitations.text: Signal change is not specific; discitis and tumour must be considered in the right context.

limitations: Changes can convert between types over time.

guideSections.what: Three types of endplate marrow change by T1/T2 signal.
guideSections.howToPerform: Compare endplate marrow signal on T1 and T2 with normal marrow; choose the type.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Correlate with symptoms; consider infection when appropriate.

sources.citation: Modic MT, Steinberg PM, Ross JS, Masaryk TJ, Carter JR. Degenerative disk disease: assessment of changes in vertebral body marrow with MR imaging. Radiology. 1988;166(1):193-199.
